Ultimate Zanzibar Travel Guide

Research-backed tips, prices, and itineraries based on what tourists actually search for — from budget to luxury, visa info to the best beaches.

Practical Info

Best Time to Visit Zanzibar

Peak Season

June to October

Sunny, cool, and dry — ideal for safaris and beach activities. July-August is the busiest.

Best Overall Month

September

Great weather with fewer crowds. Best value month for deals on accommodations.

Best Value

June and October

Bonus: fewer crowds means better access to tours and lower prices.

Avoid

March to May (long rains; April is wettest)

Some hotels close during low season. Perfect for budget travelers seeking deals.

Activities

Top Things to Do in Zanzibar

Ranked by search volume and traveler popularity.

1

Stone Town Walking Tour

Explore the UNESCO World Heritage site with a licensed guide. Visit the House of Wonders, Old Fort, Sultan's Palace, and bustling markets.

$13–$80 per person
2

Spice Farm Tour

Journey into Zanzibar's interior to a working spice farm. Taste cloves, cinnamon, vanilla, and cardamom. Learn why Zanzibar is called the "Spice Island."

$25–$57 per person
3

Safari Blue / Menai Bay Dhow Day

Zanzibar's most famous dhow excursion: cruise to Menai Bay Conservation Area, snorkel over vibrant coral reefs, feast on a seafood barbecue on a private sandbank.

$45–$160 per person
4

Mnemba Atoll Snorkeling

Snorkel the pristine waters of Mnemba Atoll, Zanzibar's premier marine conservation area. Spot green sea turtles and colorful fish over healthy coral reefs.

$50–$150 per person
5

Prison Island Tour

Visit the island famous for its giant Aldabra tortoises (some over 190 years old), coral museums, and snorkeling spots.

$50–$100 per person
6

Jozani Forest & Red Colobus

Walk through the only remaining nature reserve on Zanzibar. Spot the endangered Zanzibar red colobus monkey and learn about the mangrove ecosystem.

$25–$60 per person

Cultural Tips

Before You Go

  • Dress modestly in towns/villages (cover shoulders and knees)
  • Beachwear OK only on beaches and at resorts
  • Respect Muslim customs during Ramadan (no public eating/drinking during daylight)
  • Learn basic Swahili phrases (Jambo, Asante, Karibu, Samahani)
  • Ask permission before photographing people
  • Bargaining is expected at markets and local shops
  • Tipping 5-10% for good service is customary
  • Remove shoes when entering local homes
  • Support local communities by visiting markets, eating locally
FAQ

Travel Questions Answered

Is Zanzibar safe for tourists?

Zanzibar is generally safe for tourists, including solo female travelers. Common issues include petty theft, persistent beach vendors, and tourist hassle in busy areas. Keep valuables secure, avoid walking alone late at night, and use registered taxis or trusted drivers. In Stone Town, it's safe during the day but use registered taxis or guides after dark.

Do I need a visa for Zanzibar?

Most nationalities require a Tanzania visa (which covers Zanzibar) valid for 90 days. Apply online via the official e-visa system at https://visa.immigration.go.tz/. Your passport must be valid for at least 6 months from departure. Zanzibar also requires mandatory inbound travel insurance — apply at https://inbound.visitzanzibar.go.tz/

What is the best time to visit Zanzibar?

Peak season is June to October (cool, dry). September is the best overall month. Best value months are June and October with good weather and fewer crowds. Avoid March to May (long rains, April is wettest). July-August is the busiest. For diving and snorkeling, February-March offer the best visibility.

How many days do I need in Zanzibar?

3 nights for a quick beach break, 4-5 nights for a safari add-on plus some exploration, or 7 nights for a full island experience (Stone Town + multiple beach areas). The ideal split is 2 nights in Stone Town + 2-5 nights in a beach area.

What currency is used in Zanzibar?

The official currency is the Tanzanian Shilling (TZS). USD is widely accepted in tourist areas. Small local payments are easier in shillings — carry cash. ATMs are available in main towns and tourist areas.

Do I need malaria tablets for Zanzibar?

Malaria can occur in Zanzibar. Speak to a travel clinic for advice on anti-malaria medication before arrival. Pack insect repellent with DEET, long sleeves for evenings, and mosquito nets. The risk is lower in Stone Town and main tourist areas but higher in rural regions.

How do I get around Zanzibar?

In Stone Town, walking is the best option for short distances. For longer distances, use Zanzibus shuttles ($5-8), shared taxis (dala dalas at $1), or private taxis ($20-25/hour). Car rental is possible but driving is chaotic. Arrange airport transfers in advance through your accommodation ($10-30).
